title: Towards Hyperparameter Transfer for Differentially Private Optimization
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: A cheap proxy-model search plus principled scaling rules transfers tuned settings to large models while preserving invariant training dynamics.
layout: 4 colored panels, left-to-right with feedback loops, gear and diamond decision nodes
description: A four-stage workflow diagram drawn as rounded panels in blue, green, yellow and blue. Panel 1, 'Privacy & SNR Setup', has a lock icon for the privacy budget (ε,δ)-DP. Arrows lead to large-model noise σ_large and an SNR Condition diamond (Eq. 8), which feeds small-model noise σ_small. Panel 2, 'Small Model Proxy Search', in green, takes the clipping coefficient C_small into a small neural-net icon labeled μP Init. A grid-search box feeds an Optimal LR diamond. Panel 3, 'μP Scaling Mechanism', in yellow, has a clipping coefficient C_large box above a large gear labeled Layer-wise Scaling Law (Eq. 4). A red callout reads 'O(1) Loss Update (Invariant Dynamics)'. Panel 4, 'Large Model Execution', shows layer-wise learning rates above a large network, leading up to a flag-marked goal box. The eye starts at the top-left lock and follows the arrows across the panels.
caption: DP-$\mu$P Training Workflow. We employ $\mu$P initialization to stabilize the initial state and align the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) to derive the appropriate noise parameters for the small proxy model. After identifying the optimal base learning rate on the proxy, we apply layer-wise scaling to the large model to ensure $\mathcal{O}(1)$ loss updates, resulting in invariant training dynamics across model scales. A numerical example is provided in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Scaling laws and hyperparameter tuning remain central challenges in training large-scale models, particularly under differential privacy (DP), where optimization is further complicated by noise injection and per-sample gradient clipping. While Maximal Update Parametrization ($Î¼$P) allows for zero-shot hyperparameter transfer in standard training, we show that it fails under DP constraints due to the distinct spectral properties of high-dimensional noise versus low-rank gradients. In this work, we introduce DP-$Î¼$P, a theoretically grounded framework that extends $Î¼$P to the privacy-preserving setting. By analyzing the interaction between gradient clipping, noise injection, and feature learning, we derive a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) condition that governs layer-wise learning rate scaling. Combining this with our proposed spectral scaling formulation, we provide specific scaling rules for DP-SGD, DP-Adam, and DP-Muon optimizers. Empirically, we demonstrate that DP-$Î¼$P enables effective zero-shot transfer of learning rates across model widths on diverse architectures (MLP, ViT, GPT-2), matching or exceeding the performance of individually tuned baselines while significantly reducing computational costs.
